Definition: from G1519 and a presumed derivative of G3700; a mirror (for looking into):--glass. Compare G2734.
BiblicalUsage: ésoptron means a mirror. It occurs twice, in 1 Corinthians and James.
TheologicalSignificance: For me, ésoptron is a reminder to read plainly rather than to force a meaning.
